links.outcome: Prescription-parameter accuracy and coverage of retrieval-augmented vs base LLM medication recommendations
links.effect: All-correct prescription-parameter rate 0.948 for Retrieval-augmented LLM vs 0.494 for Base LLM; retrieval augmentation improved coverage and prescribing accuracy.
links.quote: Retrieval augmentation improved coverage and prescribing accuracy, while Physician-RAG collaborative showed the highest agreement with the expert reference standard across completeness, safety screening, prioritization, and structured prescribing quality.

links.outcome: Comparing physician alone, LLM alone, RAG alone, and physician-RAG collaboration against expert reference
links.effect: Physician-RAG had the highest CORE recall (1.000), precision (0.963), Jaccard (0.943) and lowest AVOID-hit rate (0.026); all-correct prescription rate 0.951 vs 0.945 physician and 0.494 base LLM.
links.quote: Prescription-parameter accuracy was highest in the Physician-RAG collaborative workflow (all-correct rate 0.951), compared with 0.948 for the Retrieval-augmented LLM workflow, 0.945 for the Physician workflow, and 0.494 for the Base LLM workflow.

links.outcome: Comparison of LLM workflows against physicians on same cases using reference standard
links.effect: Stand-alone LLM showed lower agreement and weaker structured prescribing accuracy than supervised workflows; Physician-RAG had the highest agreement with the expert reference.
links.quote: In this retrospective expert-reference-based evaluation, stand-alone LLM output showed lower agreement and weaker structured prescribing accuracy than supervised workflows.
